column1: 358759|complete|All lengths and all descent-top/bottom set pairs; equal avoidance counts for the three patterns.|The statistics and universal distribution comparison are specified.|PARK_BIJECTION|Needs one joint-statistic-preserving mechanism, not separate marginal Wilf equivalences; finite length checks cannot supply it.

358760|definition-dependent|Every nonempty sigma and traversable Ferrers board; existence of a preserving bijection.|Separated traversal and board ascent-bottom statistic are not defined operationally.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|Complementing an analogous descent assertion is a routine bridge if that assertion is proved; no independent full-scope bijection identified.

358862|definition-dependent|Every n; every irreducible character of S_n is regular invertible.|Regular invertibility is not defined.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|Character-degree arithmetic needs the precise integral representation-ring equation; verified n<=16 supplies no induction on all irreducibles.

358878|definition-dependent|Every n>=3 in (i), every n>=1 in (ii), exact equality exceptions.|Four partition families are named without their counting restrictions.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|Cannot design an injection or coefficient comparison without generating functions; two infinite inequalities and exact strictness must all be handled.

358924|definition-dependent|Every integer partition and every coefficient through its degree.|The specialization and normalization defining J are missing.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|A positive combinatorial formula would suffice, but cannot replace the unspecified polynomial by a familiar q-analogue.

358925|definition-dependent|Every partition; some peak index for its coefficient sequence.|J is not explicitly defined.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|Positive log-concavity implies unimodality routinely; that implication earns no outcome and does not prove either antecedent.

358974|incomplete|Every positive integer q, k=q+1; an invariant cylinder of periodic orbits.|The differential system is absent, so even an orbit equation cannot be formed.|HOLD_MISSING_SYSTEM|A uniform Sturm certificate might be small after parameter reduction; tests through 100 are neither such a reduction nor full-scope evidence.

359138|complete|For each epsilon>0, sufficiently large N admit <=N^epsilon colors avoiding every nonconstant symmetric 4-AP.|The forbidden four-point color pattern is explicit; N^{o(1)} has its usual asymptotic meaning.|PARK_ASYMPTOTIC|A fixed cyclic 3-coloring only yields a fixed positive exponent under product constructions; no subpolynomial family supplied. Metadata reference to Gowers concerns another conjecture and is not a refutation here.

359169|scope-ambiguous|All dimensions, 2<=q<=n+2, all prescribed positive chamber volumes; unique minimizing cluster.|Uniqueness needs an isometry/null-set convention; canonical cluster construction is not specified.|PARK_GEOMETRIC|Even after standard equivalences are restored, arbitrary cluster regularity and global optimality require a major chain; no small certificate route.

359314|definition-dependent|All distinct odd primes p,q; both reciprocal and trace polynomials irreducible.|Neither polynomial's coefficients nor cyclotomic factor normalization is given.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|A single mod-prime factorization certificate handles one n only; uniform prime selection and trace irreducibility remain the core obstruction.

359410|incomplete|Every dimension and every lattice in X_d; bound plus exact equality orbit.|X_d and A are unspecified, including lattice normalization.|HOLD_MISSING_DOMAIN|Without determinant-one normalization scaling changes the bound; a correction would not resolve the normalized Minkowski conjecture.

359551|incomplete|Existence of a two-copy channel satisfying all displayed conditional constraints.|The joint probability law, tau, and full domain are absent; i,j indexing also shifts.|HOLD_MISSING_LAW|Potential finite feasibility problem cannot be encoded faithfully; no replacement distribution or channel invented.

359586|complete|Every positive odd integer except 7,21 occurs as h(T), and the two exceptions never occur.|Tournament and directed Hamiltonian path count are standard unambiguous finite objects.|PARK_CONSTRUCTIVE|Ordinal sums multiply path counts, but arbitrary odd primes require an additive construction; no full odd-value generation scheme or exclusion proof identified.

359779|complete|Every m>=1 and every partition mu of m(m+1)/2; positive staircase-square Kronecker coefficient.|Staircase partitions and Kronecker coefficients are standard mathematical terms.|PARK_HARD|Requires support of all irreducibles in a tensor square, not a few shapes; finite characters and positivity for subclasses do not give full support.

359837|incomplete|All p>=1, all n>=1, allowed k; continuation of a spectral theorem.|Theorem label is blank and matrix entries, grids, and functions are absent.|HOLD_MISSING_THEOREM|Cannot test the claimed identity or preserve its multiplicities/boundary conditions without the theorem; retain row without replacement.

359854|complete|Every epsilon>0, all n and skew-corner-free S with an epsilon-dependent constant.|The forbidden triple is explicitly defined.|PARK_ASYMPTOTIC|Elementary pair counting gives far weaker bounds; existing near-linear lower example does not violate n^{1+epsilon}. No uniform structural compression found.

359858|definition-dependent|Every n>=6 and generic world-point configuration; exact cubic ED degree.|The affine variety and camera parametrization/equations are omitted.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|A finite critical-point count might falsify one generic n, but genericity and saturation/extraneous components need exact algebraic treatment.

359910|complete|Every finite G and finite simple S; equality of order and spectrum iff isomorphism.|Group order and element-order set have standard definitions.|PARK_PRIOR|A potentially classical characterization theorem needs actual published body checking; no source proof or present registry clearance obtained, and no novel route asserted.

360114|scope-ambiguous|All t>=12 and intended path sizes s; exact min(3s,2t).|The allowed s range is absent and symbols are corrupted; s=1 would need special care.|HOLD_SCOPE|A small path endpoint discrepancy would be a domain correction; no construction covering the intended two-dimensional range established.

360175|complete|There exists p0 such that every prime p>p0 has omega(2^p-1)<1.36 log p.|All arithmetic objects and the eventual universal bound are specified.|PARK_NUMBER_THEORY|Congruence restrictions on factors alone give much weaker deterministic bounds; a finite factor sweep cannot refute an unspecified eventual threshold.

360177|incomplete|Conditional on two prior conjectures, all sufficiently large prime p, for each distinct factor an odd separating exponent.|Uniform-distribution conjecture is not given; multiplicity convention for the displayed product is unclear.|HOLD_MISSING_HYPOTHESIS|Independence heuristics do not ensure every sign pattern along the sparse exponent interval; no rigorous joint error bound present.

360288|definition-dependent|Every hypercube dimension d and every target vertex; legal stacking sequence.|The distance-dependent cup move is not specified in the literal.|PARK_UNIFORM_CONSTRUCTION|Primary v1 definitions and Conjecture27 read; Theorem7 proves d<=20. Its body uses ad hoc cube levels; no uniform all-d level decomposition established.

360367|complete|Every n>=4; exact online size Ramsey number ceil(7n/5)-1.|Online Ramsey number and paths are standard objects with a precise formula.|PARK_KNOWN_PLUS_FINITE|Literal reports an existing proof for n>=10; the remaining six parameter values are instances, not an independent full-scope discovery mechanism. No claim of checking their game trees.

360447|complete|Every odd integer >8 except21; existence of prime plus equal-divisor-sum number.|Zumkeller is explicitly defined.|PARK_ADDITIVE|Residue-class reduction leaves infinitely many 18k+3 inputs; finite divisor-subset checks cannot close that class without a prime-producing covering argument.

360607|definition-dependent|Every b in each stated interval, and the entire sequence n>=1; all four monotonicity clauses.|L_n and R_n sampling interval/conventions are omitted from the literal.|PARK_ANALYSIS|Primary Conjecture3.2 confirms the uncovered intervals. Nearby proved ranges do not subsume them. Exact rational finite checks are instances only; b=2 left sums are already handled in Remark3.3.

360793|scope-ambiguous|Existence of c(d) with an iff involving k and instability for all n>=k+2, restricted to Fano blowups.|Placement of the universal n quantifier and behavior when no Fano blowup exists need clarification.|PARK_GEOMETRIC|A numerical threshold for n<=1000 gives no iff for unbounded n; would need exact divisor-volume formulas and both stable/unstable directions.

360889|scope-ambiguous|Each cscK class and each initial metric; existence for all iteration indices and convergence.|Tau range and topology/modulo-automorphism convention are omitted.|HOLD_REPORTED_RESOLUTION|Literal itself reports source confirmation modulo automorphisms. That is a strong prior objection, not audited proof-body clearance; no new result proposed.

360942|complete|All n,k>=0; cardinality of inversion-k 1324 avoiders nondecreasing with n.|Avoidance and inversion count specify the finite sets.|PARK_INJECTION|Appending a maximum creates new 1324 patterns from existing132 occurrences; appending a minimum changes inversion count. Neither simple extension is a full-scope injection.

361102|definition-dependent|All fifteen sequences, primes>=5 and m,r>=1; indicated powers p^{lambda r}.|The fifteen recurrences or binomial definitions are absent.|HOLD_REPORTED_RESOLUTION|Literal reports the final case proved by the source. No proof-body audit performed; re-formalizing it or reproving a special sequence earns no discovery credit.

361183|definition-dependent|All d,k>=2; both secant varieties attain expected dimension.|Moment varieties are not specified by coordinates/parametrizations.|PARK_ALGEBRAIC|Exact Jacobian rank at one tuple proves one d,k, not a uniform nondefectiveness mechanism; needs uniform tangent-space independence and saturation cases.

361333|complete|There exists c>0 for all d>=4,n,G; density implies a d-vertex linear subgraph with >=d^2/100 edges.|Linear 3-graph condition and all quantifiers are given.|PARK_EXTREMAL|Greedy removal loses control over the prescribed d-vertex density; finite small d checks do not give one absolute c for all d.

361389|scope-ambiguous|Every nonsquare v>=10^13 has a coprime numerator with the displayed restricted continued fraction.|Whether n=0 is allowed is unstated; prefix length changes the family.|PARK_THIN_ORBIT|Even under either convention, every large nonsquare denominator is a thin-semigroup coverage assertion. Congruence tests cannot prove exact eventual coverage.

361475|definition-dependent|Every staircase Kunz numerical semigroup with k=3; associated face has <=4 facets.|Staircase/Kunz construction, k and F_N are not defined.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|Counterexamples for arbitrary lattice ideals cannot be imported without verifying numerical-semigroup realizability; no faithful small certificate encoded.

361526|definition-dependent|Every k>=2; two strict expressiveness separations for Local k-FGNN.|The architectures and graph distinguishability relation are not specified.|HOLD_DEFINITIONS|A pair of graphs for one k is an instance; uniform simulation and separating families are both necessary.

361565|complete|Every n and symmetric convex body; volume(K)^2/det Cov(K)>=12^n.|Convex body covariance has its standard uniform-volume convention.|PARK_HARD|Cube equality checks are routine instances; arbitrary-dimensional extremality needs a global affine-invariant inequality, no short route identified.

361612|complete|Every prime p=1 mod4; Legendre character of an integer square root equals the displayed expression.|Determinant and characters are explicit; sign choice is immaterial since (-1/p)=1.|PARK_CHARACTER_IDENTITY|Primary Conjecture4.3 read. Pfaffian structure explains squareness but not the requested Legendre character; exact p=5 check gives only an instance.

361613|complete|Every positive odd m; finitely many primes p=1 mod4 divide D_p^(m), plus exact four listed sets.|Determinant and E(m) are explicit.|PARK_FINITE_EXCEPTION|Need a uniform algebraic bound on exceptional primes for each m; finitely many tested p cannot prove finiteness or exhaust the named sets.

361636|scope-ambiguous|Every integer q>1; prime numerator with all partial quotients<=5, and <=4 except6,54,150.|Prime residue could mean a least positive prime representative or a residue class with some prime representative; continued-fraction endpoint convention omitted.|HOLD_SCOPE|At q=2 the literal prime numerator reading already fails, indicating a convention issue rather than an eligible new counterexample; no domain correction credited.

361731|definition-dependent|Every finite prime set S, p outside S; equality of loci at all sufficiently large depths.|Refined minimal Chabauty-Kim locus construction is omitted.|PARK_DEEP|Uniform depth control requires p-adic/motivic dependencies; testing auxiliary primes for one S does not address all finite S.

361791|complete|Every bridgeless cubic G and each of four named abelian groups; zero-sum proper nonzero edge coloring.|Both proper coloring and group constraints are explicit.|PARK_COLORING|Implication from Z4xZ2 to other groups reduces targets but does not construct that first coloring; finite graph search alone lacks all-graph mechanism.

361855|scope-ambiguous|For every prime, distinct trace15-tuples on intended generic nonsingular parameters.|Five curve equations, generic excluded set, and parameter equivalence are unspecified.|HOLD_SCOPE|Without quotient convention repeated parametrizations produce artificial collisions; a trace collision is not a counterexample until geometric equivalences are fixed.

361873|complete|Every prime d=1 mod4; fundamental-unit omega coefficient not divisible by d.|Field, integral basis, unit, and divisibility predicate are specified despite TeX corruption.|PARK_NUMBER_THEORY|A Pell equation computation at a large d is only an instance; no construction of a violating prime or uniform nondivisibility argument identified.

361981|scope-ambiguous|All intended X,phi,psi and prime oriented knots through12; enhancement of Phi by Psi.|Enhancement meaning and compatibility of arbitrary cocycles are unstated.|HOLD_SCOPE|Primary Conjecture4.2 repeats arbitrary cocycles; zero cocycle can discard information. That suggests a wording/compatibility defect, not a justified new invariant theorem.

362013|incomplete|Existence of two parameter endpoints, every t between them, a unique non-equilateral unit-area orbit triangle.|Maps q_t,r_t and equivalence of triangles are absent; endpoints only approximate.|HOLD_MISSING_MAPS|An interval algebraic certificate would need exact maps, endpoint equations and uniqueness modulo symmetries; numeric phase portraits do not supply them.

362159|definition-dependent|Every prime except7; truncated fivefold multinomial sum equals a_p modulo p^2.|Three initial coefficients do not explicitly define the particular modular form.|PARK_MODULAR|Exact small-prime agreement cannot prove a modular supercongruence; need identification of the form and Frobenius/modular mechanism.

362160|scope-ambiguous|Every prime except3; four-binomial truncated sum equals a_p modulo p^3.|Prime2 is not excluded although -1/8 is not 2-adically integral; form also only partially named.|HOLD_DOMAIN|A p=2 denominator problem is a domain correction, not eligible refutation. All odd-prime mod-p^3 scope still requires substantial modular machinery.

362278|definition-dependent|Every n>=1; stated exact second quotient of tiling numbers.|Benzel geometry and allowed stones/bones are not defined.|PARK_ENUMERATION|Product-form algebra verifies a proposed formula only after an independent tiling enumeration; compression alone is no count proof.

362280|definition-dependent|Every n>=1 for the shifted benzel family; stated exact rational second quotient.|Region and tile definitions absent.|PARK_ENUMERATION|Same need for full enumeration, separately for shifted boundary; no credit for quotient arithmetic or extrapolating data.

362389|complete|Every nondegenerate finite projective plane; order must be a prime power.|Projective plane and order are standard finite-incidence objects.|PARK_HARD|Bruck-Ryser type necessary conditions do not exclude every non-prime-power order; no small all-order certificate mechanism.

362520|definition-dependent|Every pair of finite trees; equality of the q-leading invariant implies isomorphism.|q-chromatic normalization and whether leading is in x or q are not explicit.|PARK_TREE_INVARIANT|Finite trees through17 give no reconstruction theorem; requires a uniform recovery mechanism or actual nonisomorphic pair with exact invariant equality.
